classification.difficultyReason: Distinguishes a specified sequence from a cumulative count of rainy days.

content.prompt: During winter it rains on average 18 out of 30 days. Five winter days are selected at random. Find, correct to four decimal places, the probability that:

children.label: a
children.prompt: the first two days chosen will be fine and the remainder wet,

answer.worked:
Use $P(\text{wet})=\frac{18}{30}=0.6$ and $P(\text{fine})=0.4$, treating the selected days as independent.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{first two fine, next three wet})&=(0.4)^2(0.6)^3\\&=0.03456\\&\approx0.0346.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: more rainy days than fine days have been chosen.

answer.worked:
Let $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(5,0.6)$ count rainy days, treating the selected days as independent. More rainy days than fine days means $X\ge3$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X\ge3)&=\sum_{x=3}^{5}\binom{5}{x}(0.6)^x(0.4)^{5-x}\\&=10(0.6)^3(0.4)^2+5(0.6)^4(0.4)+(0.6)^5\\&=0.68256\\&\approx0.6826.\end{aligned}$$
